reason: While some regular people (judges and Levites) are portrayed favorably in the reforms section, the prominent regular people in the narrative—the four hundred prophets—are portrayed very unfavorably as speakers of falsehoods, recipients of a lying spirit ('רוּחַ שֶׁקֶר'), and deceivers who oppose the true prophet Micaiah. The narrative emphasizes their moral corruption and unfaithfulness to God's truth. The overall treatment of regular people is mixed rather than consistently favorable.
